sheet-2.description: The business centre of Bernardsville around Olcott Square, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned about 90 degrees from north, so that north points to the left of the page and Morristown Road runs up the sheet. Anderson Hill Road crosses the middle from the left edge to Olcott Square, where Morristown Road, Mount Airy Road and Mine Brook Road meet. Church Lane closes the block at the top and Westley Avenue runs down the left edge. Public and institutional buildings stand along Morristown Road north of the square: the Masonic Temple, Arcanum Hall, the Public Library and the printing works of the Bernardsville News. South and east of the square the blocks are commercial and densely built: the Old Stone Hotel, the Liberty Picture Theatre, the Borough Hall and council rooms, Bernards Inn with bowling and billiards, a bakery, stores with flats above, and several auto sales rooms and a large garage along Quimby Lane. Mill Street leads down to the H. N. Miller feed mill, a creamery and the fire department, with Mine Brook crossing the lower part of the sheet from left to right. The Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railway runs through the upper right corner, crossing Mount Airy Road on an iron bridge, with a substation of the railway company beside Mine Brook Road. Water pipes of four and six inches run along the street centres. The left half above Anderson Hill Road is mostly large undeveloped lots with scattered dwellings. Claremont Road and Essex Avenue are printed along the bottom edge, and the numbers of the neighbouring sheets (3, 4, 5, 6, 12) are printed at the edges.
notes: Church Lane is today Church Street; Westley Avenue is today Wesley Avenue; Mill is today Mill Street; Boylan Terrace and Mount Airy Road keep their names.
Anderson Hill Road, Morristown Road and Olcott Square have been reshaped since 1930: the modern Olcott Square nodes do not match the drawn square, so no point was taken there.
The sheet is turned: the compass rose at the top right shows north pointing to the left.
50 ft. Business centre: Mine Brook Road, Olcott Square, Anderson Hill Road, Claremont Road, Quimby Lane, Mill Street. One part.

sheet-3.description: The western edge of Bernardsville's business district, between Morris Avenue along the top of the sheet and Mine Brook Road along the bottom, with Depot Place on the west and Claremont Road on the east. Somerset Avenue and Essex Avenue cross the sheet from west-south-west to east-north-east, and Passaic Avenue and Seney Avenue run north from them. Most of the sheet is residential: frame dwellings with stables and auto houses on large lots, several of them with lot numbers and house numbers along the street fronts. The south-east corner is commercial and industrial and is drawn densely: the contractor and mill work shop of Chas. Pfadenhauer, a storage warehouse for household goods, two public garages, auto sales and auto repair shops, the post office, a bank and the telephone exchange along Claremont Road and the north side of Mine Brook Road. Across Mine Brook Road in the south-east corner are a small park, the tracks of the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad and a stream. Water pipes of four and six inches are drawn in most streets with their hydrants. Block numbers (204, 206, 207, 208, 108, 109, 50, 51, 52) and the numbers of the adjoining sheets (2, 4, 12, 15) are printed at the edges. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and is turned about 13 degrees from north.
notes: Seney Avenue is today Stevens Street (the modern Seney Drive is further north-east).
Depot Place is today Woodland Road; the modern Depot Place is a short street by the station east of Claremont Road.
Passaic Avenue is today Passaic Street.
Mine Brook Road has been realigned near Depot Place since 1930.
50 ft. Pilot. Morris, Somerset, Essex Avs, Passaic Av (Passaic Street), Seney Av (now Stevens Street), Depot Pl (now Woodland Road), Claremont Rd, Mine Brook Rd. One part.

sheet-4.description: A mostly residential and open district immediately north of Bernardsville's business centre, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north roughly at the top. Claremont Road crosses the sheet from the upper left to the bottom centre, with Seney Drive leaving it at the top and Mine Mount Road running east from the same junction to Anderson Hill Road, which follows the right-hand edge. Booner and Mine Mount Place branch north and south from Mine Mount Road. A creek enters under a culvert at Mine Mount Road and winds south-east through the middle of the sheet, bordered by large undivided lots. Along Mine Mount Road and Mine Mount Place the lots are narrow and carry frame dwellings with outbuildings, an upholstery shop and a tin smith's store. The two St. Bernards Episcopal Church buildings and their parish house stand west of Claremont Road, on a large open lot, with a compass rose and north arrow beside them. Two streets, drawn in dashed outline and marked Not Open, are laid out across the open land east of the creek. At the lower left a small block of dwellings lies between Seney Avenue and Morris Avenue, and Claremont Road divides into a narrower branch near the bottom of the sheet. Water pipes of four and six inches follow Seney Drive, Claremont Road and Anderson Hill Road. The adjoining sheets 2, 3, 5, 7 and 10 are named at the edges.
notes: Booner is today Bodnar Street.
Mine Mount Place appears to be today's Park Lane, which is not joined to Mine Mount Road in OpenStreetMap.
Seney Avenue is today Stevens Street; Mill is today Mill Street.
Control rests on three junctions along Mine Mount Road and two hand-picked junctions to the south, so placement of the lower half is uncertain.
50 ft. Claremont Rd, Mine Mount Pl/Rd, Anderson Hill Rd, Seney Av; creek. One part.

sheet-5.description: A residential district east of Anderson Hill Road, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north at the top. Anderson Hill Road runs down the left edge of the sheet; Highview Avenue and Olcott Avenue leave it to the north-east and Westley Avenue leaves it to the east, so that the three avenues fan out across the sheet. Highview Avenue and Olcott Avenue are lined with frame dwellings and outbuildings on deep lots, many of them with house numbers. In the middle, on the north side of Olcott Avenue, stands the Public School, and east of it a very large pink building, drawn in brick, occupies the right-hand edge; an athletic field is lettered across the open land to the north-east. At the bottom of the sheet Westley Avenue sweeps round in a loop that encloses the M. E. Church and its parsonage, with Church Lane entering from the bottom edge and Dawnley Lane running off to the south-east. An auto repair shop and several small stores stand beside Anderson Hill Road at the upper left. Water pipes of four and six inches are drawn along the main streets and their hydrants and hose houses are marked at the school. Much of the right half of the sheet is blank, left open for the adjoining sheets 6 and 7. A compass rose and north arrow stand at the right. Sheets 2, 4, 6, 7 and 8 are named around the edges.
notes: Westley Avenue is today Wesley Avenue; Dawnley Lane is today Dawnleigh Lane; Church Lane is today Church Street.
The modern junction of Dawnleigh Lane and High School Lane lies about 12 m from the drawn junction at the end of Westley Avenue and was left out of the fit.

Control is four junctions: three along Anderson Hill Road, which is a boundary street drawn on this sheet from its east edge only, and one at Church Lane, so the east side of the sheet is placed by extension.
50 ft. Olcott Av, Westley Av, Highview Av, Anderson Hill Rd. One part.

sheet-6-1.description: A thinly built residential district on the north-east side of Bernardsville, bounded by Church Lane on the west and Morristown Road along the bottom of the sheet. Westley Avenue leaves Church Lane northward and a second branch of it runs north-north-east to Dawnley Lane, a narrow lane that runs east-south-east across the middle of the sheet. The upper half of the sheet is the grounds of the High School, a large brick building with gymnasium, stage, auditorium and balcony, drawn without surrounding streets, and a smaller Public School of concrete block nearer Dawnley Lane. The lower half has frame dwellings, auto houses and stables on irregular lots between Church Lane, Westley Avenue and Morristown Road, among them a small store and an auto repair shop near the corner of Church Lane and Morristown Road. Water pipes are drawn in Church Lane, Westley Avenue and Morristown Road. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and is turned about 5 degrees anticlockwise. The top-right corner of the sheet is a separate inset of Morristown Road further east (part 2) and is not part of this area; block numbers 5 and 8 and the numbers of the adjoining sheets 2, 5, 8 and 11 are printed at the edges.
notes: Church Lane is today Church Street.
Westley Avenue is today Wesley Avenue (west and south of the bend) and the south end of High School Lane (the branch north to Dawnley Lane).
Dawnley Lane is today Dawnleigh Lane.
The modern junction of Wesley Avenue and High School Lane lies about 13 m east of where the sheet draws the fork; it was not used as control.

50 ft. Two parts: 1 main map, rotation about -5 deg (Church Lane = Church Street, Westley Av = Wesley Avenue and the south end of High School Lane, Dawnley Lane = Dawnleigh Lane, Morristown Rd; High School and Public School); 2 top-right inset of the north frontage of Morristown Rd (Virginia Day Nursery), no junction.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: top-right inset: north frontage of Morristown Road with the Virginia Day Nursery summer home (no street junction (Morristown Road and a lot line only); needs carried points from sheet-11 part 2 or sheet-6 part 1 if a shared feature can be identified, or parcel corners).

sheet-7.description: The north-western edge of Bernardsville, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the top, slightly to the left. Seney Drive runs up the sheet from the lower left to the top, with Anderson Hill Road forming the diagonal edge to its right, so that the built-up land is a wedge narrowing towards the top. Mine Mount Road crosses the bottom of the sheet from Claremont Road at the left to Mine Mount Place and beyond; Booner, also lettered as North Mine Mount Road, climbs from it between narrow lots and bends to meet Anderson Hill Road. A creek crosses Seney Drive under a stone bridge and runs south to a culvert under Mine Mount Road. The left side of the sheet is institutional: the Our Lady of Perpetual Help R. C. Church with its rectory, a convent, a long shed, and the Elizabeth Jane Hamilton Brady Memorial Buildings with the parochial school and auditorium, drawn in brick, all standing in open grounds with a playground lettered above them. East of Seney Drive the blocks are divided into narrow lots with frame dwellings and outbuildings, and a larger block of dwellings along Anderson Hill Road at the right. Old Army Road appears at the right edge. Water pipes of four inches follow Seney Drive and Claremont Road. A compass rose at the upper right shows north tilted to the left of the page. The left part of the sheet is blank and belongs to sheet 10.
notes: Booner (North Mine Mount Road) is today Bodnar Street.
Mine Mount Place appears to be today's Park Lane.

The three junctions that fix the placement are Claremont Road with Mine Mount Road and Seney Drive, Booner with Mine Mount Road (hand-picked) and Anderson Hill Road with Booner (the end of the diagonal lane, approximate), so the fit is exact and has no check.
The compass rose shows north tilted about 18 degrees to the left, which does not agree with the fitted rotation.
50 ft. Seney Drive, Booner, Anderson Hill Rd, Mine Mount Rd; Catholic church. One part.

sheet-8.description: A residential district on the north-east side of Bernardsville, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the left of the page, as the compass rose at the left shows. Anderson Hill Road runs along the bottom of the sheet. Old Army Road, also lettered Childs Avenue, descends from the upper left towards it, and Highview Avenue runs parallel to it on the right, while Elmer Avenue and Ford Avenue cross both from the lower left to the upper right. Olcott Avenue closes the top of the sheet, with Bell Terrace and Childsworth Avenue leaving it at the top and upper right. The blocks are divided into narrow, deep lots with house numbers, and almost every lot holds a frame dwelling with an outbuilding. Only a few buildings are drawn in other colours: a pink building near the centre, a pink-bordered dwelling and a small blue building beside Anderson Hill Road. The upper left and the centre are blank or only partly built, with block numbers 102 and 103, and the left edge is open for neighbouring sheets. Water pipes of four and six inches are drawn along Olcott Avenue, Highview Avenue and Anderson Hill Road, with hydrants marked at several points. Sheets 5, 6, 7 and 9 are named around the edges.
notes: Old Army Road is lettered with Childs Avenue in brackets.
Elmer is today Elmer Avenue.
The sheet is turned: the compass rose shows north pointing left.

Control is six junctions placed by hand or from edge pairs (the detector did not find any on its own from the lot lines); three of them (Ford with Old Army Road and Highview Avenue, Anderson Hill Road with Old Army Road) are approximate, as the streets are drawn only by lot lines.
50 ft. Old Army Rd, Elmer Av, Ford Av, Highview Av, Anderson Hill Rd, Olcott Av. One part.

sheet-9-1.description: A residential district on the north side of Bernardsville around Mullen Lane. Olcott Avenue runs down the west edge of the sheet and Old Army Road leaves it north-eastward at the top left. Highview Avenue, Bell Terrace and Childsworth Avenue run north-east from Olcott Avenue and are crossed by Mullen Lane, which runs south-east from Old Army Road across the middle of the sheet. The blocks are divided into regular house lots with frame dwellings, auto houses and a few stables; one brick dwelling stands on Childsworth Avenue. Much of the east half of the sheet is open land (block 213) with no buildings. Lot and house numbers are printed along the streets, and water pipes are drawn in Olcott Avenue and Old Army Road. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north about 6 degrees to the right of the top. A heavy line cuts off the bottom-right corner, which holds a separate inset of Old Army Road and Highview Avenue north-east of Mullen Lane (part 2). Block numbers 102, 104, 105, 106, 212 and 213 and the numbers of the adjoining sheets 7, 8 and 9 are printed on the sheet.
notes: Mullen Lane is today Mullens Lane.
The fitted scale (about 7.9 px/ft) is a few percent smaller than the atlas's other 50 ft sheets.

50 ft (fits about 7.9 px/ft, a few percent small). Two parts: 1 main map (Olcott Av, Old Army Rd, Highview Av, Mullen Lane = Mullens Lane, Bell Ter, Childsworth Av); 2 bottom-right inset of Old Army Rd and Highview Av north-east of Mullen Lane.

sheet-9-2.description: An inset in the bottom-right corner of sheet 9, separated from the main map by a heavy line. It shows Old Army Road and Highview Avenue running north-east, parallel to each other, from Mullen Lane, which crosses the bottom of the inset towards the south-east. The inset continues the main map beyond its top edge, where Old Army Road leaves the sheet. The land between the two roads is block 212, with three frame dwellings with attics and basements facing Old Army Road; the rest of the inset is open land. Old Army Road is drawn 50 feet wide with a six-inch water pipe and a hydrant, Mullen Lane 40 feet and Highview Avenue 50 feet. The north arrow for the sheet stands at the top of the inset, and a note marks the north side as an exposure. The inset is drawn at the same scale (50 feet to an inch) and the same orientation as the main map.
notes: Mullen Lane is today Mullens Lane.
Highview Avenue no longer continues north-east of Mullens Lane.
Placed from one detected junction (Mullens Lane / Old Army Road) with the scale of part 1 and the rotation of the measured street lines; low confidence.

50 ft (fits about 7.9 px/ft, a few percent small). Two parts: 1 main map (Olcott Av, Old Army Rd, Highview Av, Mullen Lane = Mullens Lane, Bell Ter, Childsworth Av); 2 bottom-right inset of Old Army Rd and Highview Av north-east of Mullen Lane.

sheet-10-1.description: The north-west edge of Bernardsville along Claremont Road, drawn turned on the page so that north points to the right. Mine Mount Road runs down the left edge of the sheet, Claremont Road crosses the sheet diagonally from Mine Mount Road at the bottom left to the top, and Thompson, a short 30-foot street, runs from Claremont Road towards Mine Mount Road and stops short of it. Seney Avenue meets Mine Mount Road from the left. A creek runs down the middle of the sheet and crosses Claremont Road. Thompson is lined with small frame dwellings on narrow lots; the other blocks hold frame dwellings, auto houses and stables on larger lots, a blacksmith shop near Claremont Road, and a group of buildings beside the creek including an auto repair garage and a tile-roofed store. Water pipes of four and six inches are drawn in Thompson, Claremont Road and Mine Mount Road. A heavy line divides the sheet: the area to the right of it is a separate part showing Claremont Road further north at Mendham Road (part 2). Block numbers 1, 4, 5 and 203 and the numbers of the adjoining sheets 4, 7 and 10 are printed on the sheet, which is drawn at 50 feet to an inch.
notes: Seney Avenue is today Stevens Street; its junction with Mine Mount Road is about 20 percent further from Claremont Road today than drawn and was not used as control.
Thompson is today Thompson Street.
Placed from two hand-picked junctions (Claremont Road / Thompson Street and Claremont Road / Mine Mount Road) as a helmert; low confidence.

50 ft. Turned on the page: north points right (rotation about +85 to +89 deg). Two parts divided by a heavy line: 1 main map (Mine Mount Rd, Thompson, Claremont Rd, Seney Av = Stevens Street, creek); 2 Claremont Rd north to Mendham Rd (and Olcott Lane).

sheet-10-2.description: The right-hand part of sheet 10, separated from the main map by a heavy line and drawn, like it, with north pointing to the right. It shows Claremont Road running from the bottom of the sheet north to its junction with Mendham Road, which leaves to the east along the top right, and with the road that continues Claremont Road northward beyond the junction. A Private Road runs parallel to Mendham Road between the lots. The blocks (numbered 1, 201, 202 and 203) are large residential lots with frame dwellings, auto houses and stables, most of them set well back from Claremont Road, and much open ground. Claremont Road is drawn 50 feet wide with a six-inch water pipe and a hydrant; Mendham Road is 45 feet and the Private Road 30 feet. The house numbers along Claremont Road run from about 510 to 522. The sheet's north arrow and scale bar stand in this part, which is drawn at 50 feet to an inch.
notes: The continuation of Claremont Road north of Mendham Road is today Olcott Lane.
Placed from one detected junction (Claremont Road / Mendham Road / Olcott Lane) with an assumed scale of 8.08 px/ft and the rotation of the measured street lines; low confidence.

50 ft. Turned on the page: north points right (rotation about +85 to +89 deg). Two parts divided by a heavy line: 1 main map (Mine Mount Rd, Thompson, Claremont Rd, Seney Av = Stevens Street, creek); 2 Claremont Rd north to Mendham Rd (and Olcott Lane).

sheet-11-1.description: The lower of two strips on sheet 11, separated by a heavy line: Morristown Road along the east side of Bernardsville from a little west of Finley Avenue, which crosses the right edge of the strip. The upper strip of the sheet continues the road westward. The south side of Morristown Road holds the yard of the Bernards Builders' Supply Co. (office and show room, sash and door storage, lumber storage, lime and cement), served by sidings of the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad that curve across the bottom of the strip to a concrete coal trestle, with lumber piles beside the tracks. Further east are frame dwellings, an office, and the buildings of the Hoffman Construction Co. near Finley Avenue. Morristown Road is drawn 60 feet wide, with a six-inch water pipe that turns into Finley Avenue. Block number 13 and the numbers of the adjoining sheets 8, 11 and 13 are printed in the strip, which is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned about 19 degrees.
notes: Placed from one hand-picked junction (Finley Avenue / Morristown Road) with an assumed scale of 8.08 px/ft and north from the drawn street directions (19 degrees); low confidence.

50 ft. Two horizontal strips divided by a heavy line, rotation about 18-19 deg: 1 lower strip, Morristown Rd west of Finley Ave (Hoffman Construction Co., Bernards Builders Supply Co.); 2 upper strip, Morristown Rd, D.L.&W. R.R. and Conkling Lumber Co. down to Prospect at Washington Ave. One junction each.

sheet-11-2.description: The upper of two strips on sheet 11, separated by a heavy line: the land between Morristown Road along the top and Prospect at the bottom, on the east side of Bernardsville, crossed by the tracks of the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad. The yard of the Conkling Lumber Co. lies along the tracks, with long lumber sheds, a coal pocket on a trestle, a planked driveway, lumber piles and board fences. Near Morristown Road are an auto repair garage with underground gasoline tanks, a lime, cement, sash and blind warehouse and an office with scales beside a driveway. The area between the railroad and Prospect is mostly open, with a few frame dwellings, and the west edge is marked as vacant woods. Washington Avenue leaves Prospect southward at the bottom left. Block numbers 13 and 14 and the numbers of the adjoining sheets 6, 8 and 11 are printed in the strip, which is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned about 18 degrees; the lower strip of the sheet continues it eastward.
notes: Prospect is today Prospect Street.
Placed from one hand-picked junction (Prospect Street / Washington Avenue) with an assumed scale of 8.08 px/ft and north from the drawn street directions (18 degrees); low confidence.

50 ft. Two horizontal strips divided by a heavy line, rotation about 18-19 deg: 1 lower strip, Morristown Rd west of Finley Ave (Hoffman Construction Co., Bernards Builders Supply Co.); 2 upper strip, Morristown Rd, D.L.&W. R.R. and Conkling Lumber Co. down to Prospect at Washington Ave. One junction each.

sheet-12.description: The south-eastern part of Bernardsville's town centre, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned about 62 degrees so that north points to the upper left, as the compass rose shows. Mount Airy Road, Centre Street and West Street cross the sheet from side to side, and Prospect Street runs between them from top to bottom, with Boylan Terrace along the left side beside the tracks of the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad and Highland Avenue at the right edge. The blocks between the cross streets are divided into narrow lots with frame dwellings and outbuildings; larger lots at the right are mostly open. Between Mount Airy Road and Centre Street, along Boylan Terrace, stand a private garage with an office belonging to the New Jersey Power and Light Company, with a transformer enclosure, and an auto repair building in blue. A long private building and several dwellings stand in the next block. The passenger station of the railroad is at the lower left, between the main tracks and a siding, and a stream crosses the tracks beside it. At the bottom, on West Street, are the Bernards Township storehouse and a storage building, with a store and dwellings. Water pipes of four and six inches are drawn along every street. Block numbers 13 to 19 and the neighbouring sheets 2 and 3 are printed on the sheet.
notes: Prospect is today West Prospect Street (it joins Prospect Street at Mount Airy Road); Centre is today Center Street; West is today West Street.
The sheet is turned: the compass rose shows north pointing up and to the left.
50 ft. Boylan Terrace, Center, Mt. Airy Rd, West, Prospect, D.L.&W. R.R. One part.

sheet-13.description: The south-eastern part of Bernardsville's residential district, around the meeting of Mount Airy Road, Dayton, Burrows and Bernards Avenue. The sheet is turned: north points towards the left side of the page, so Bernards Avenue runs from the middle of the sheet down towards the bottom-left corner and Mount Airy Road crosses the middle from left to right. Highland Avenue runs down the left side, Dobbs runs north from Mount Airy Road, and Dayton and Burrows lie in the upper right. Centre and West cross Bernards Avenue lower on the sheet, and the south-east corner reaches High. Nearly all of the sheet is dwellings, mostly two-storey frame houses with auto houses and sheds on lots of 40 to 50 feet frontage, with house numbers along the street fronts. The one industrial property is Joseph Dobbs Inc., woodworking with power and lights electric, with a long lumber shed beside it, at the top between Dobbs and Dayton. A concrete auto house is drawn in blue on the west side lower down. Water pipes of four and six inches are drawn in most streets with hydrants. A compass rose at the top shows the turned orientation. Block numbers 118, 119, 120, 121 and 219 are printed in the blocks, and the large numerals 12 and 14 at the margins mark the neighbouring sheets. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and carries the September 1930 Bernardsville stamp.
notes: The sheet is turned: the fit gives a rotation of about -69 degrees, north pointing towards the left of the page.
Centre is today Center Street, Dobbs is Dobbs Street, Dayton is Dayton Street, Burrows is Burrows Avenue and West is West Street.
High is today Hill Street (identified by position along Bernards Avenue, not by name).
Highland Avenue is not in the modern street data under that name.
Placed from five junctions along Bernards Avenue, Mount Airy Road, Dobbs and Dayton; the fit has no points in the upper left or lower right.
50 ft. Mt. Airy Rd, Highland, Dobbs, Dayton, Burrows, Centre. One part.

sheet-14.description: The area south-west of the centre of Bernardsville, on both sides of Bernards Avenue. The sheet is turned, with north towards the left of the page, so Bernards Avenue runs down the middle of the sheet and Mine Brook Avenue runs parallel to it down the left side. High, West, Somerset, Maple and Grove cross the sheet from top to bottom in that order, High at the head of the sheet and Grove at the foot. Most of the sheet is dwellings, many of them with auto houses and sheds, on lots of 40 to 50 feet, with house numbers printed along the streets. Two churches are drawn: the Italian R.C. Church, in pink, on the west side of Bernards Avenue between West and Maple, with heat by steam and electric light, and the Italian Evangl. Church, in blue, on the east side near Maple. A warehouse and several small shops stand on the north side of Maple at the corner of Bernards Avenue. A row of five small cottages numbered 6 to 14 stands on the south side of Grove, and a row of attached dwellings on Bernards Avenue near the foot of the sheet. Two dwellings north of Somerset are marked From Plans. Several streets are drawn with four-inch and six-inch water pipes. Block numbers 111 to 117 are printed in the blocks and the numeral 13 at the top edge marks the sheet to the north-east. The compass rose at the head of the sheet shows the turned orientation. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch.
notes: The sheet is turned: the fit gives a rotation of about -85 degrees, north pointing towards the left of the page.
Mine Brook Avenue is today Mine Avenue (placed by position; the modern Mine Brook Road is elsewhere).
High is today Hill Street, Somerset is Garibaldi Street, Maple is Maple Street, Grove is Grove Street and West is West Street (identified by position along Bernards Avenue, not by name).
Two dwellings north of Somerset are labelled From Plans.
Placed from seven junctions on Bernards Avenue, Maple, Grove and West; the Somerset and Mine Brook Avenue junction was not detected.
50 ft. Mine Brook Av, Bernards Av, Maple, Grove, Somerset, High. One part.

sheet-15-3.description: The bottom-left part of sheet 15, separated from the other parts by heavy lines: Mine Brook Road near the Bernardsville station, where Depot Place comes down to it from the north. Between Mine Brook Road and a creek along the bottom of the part lie the freight yard and the businesses served by the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad: the railroad's freight house of reinforced concrete, the ice, hay and feed buildings of Barker & Higgins with an ice house and platform, an auto sales room and a garage on Mine Brook Road, the coal dump, hay storage, warehouse, electrical supplies and feed buildings of the Bernardsville Supply Co., a sub-station of the N. J. Power & Light Co., and the pump house of the Standard Oil Co. with oil tanks beyond. Several tracks and sidings cross the part from west to east. A few frame dwellings and a storage shed stand west of the yard. Water pipes are drawn in Mine Brook Road and Depot Place. Block number 19 and the number of the adjoining sheet 3 are printed in the part, which is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned about 14 degrees.
notes: Depot Place is today Woodland Road.
Placed from one detected junction (Mine Brook Road / Woodland Road) with an assumed scale of 8.08 px/ft and the rotation of the measured street lines; low confidence.

50 ft. Four parts divided by heavy lines: 1 top-left, Mine Brook Rd and the mill pond west of town (no junction); 2 top-right, Hoffman Construction Co. quarry (no street); 3 bottom-left, Mine Brook Rd at Depot Pl with the D.L.&W. freight house; 4 bottom-right, Essex Av at Chilton (drawn about 26 deg; its north arrow shows about 7 deg, the streets 26).

Not georeferenced on this sheet: top-left: Mine Brook Road and the mill pond and dam west of town (no street junction; Mine Brook Road and the railroad run parallel without meeting; needs hand placement against aerial imagery (pond, dam) or parcel corners).
Not georeferenced on this sheet: top-right: Hoffman Construction Co. quarry buildings (no street drawn).

sheet-15-4.description: The bottom-right part of sheet 15, separated from the other parts by heavy lines: the west end of Essex Avenue where Chilton comes down to it from the south, on the west side of Bernardsville. Essex Avenue runs across the part from left to right and Chilton runs down from it to the bottom edge; both are drawn 50 feet wide with four-inch water pipes. The blocks on either side (50, 51 and 110) are divided into residential lots with frame dwellings, some with attics and basements, and small auto houses of concrete block. The part is drawn at 50 feet to an inch. It is drawn with Essex Avenue square across the page; its own north arrow points only a few degrees to the right of the top, but the street directions put north about 26 degrees to the right, and the part was placed with that rotation.
notes: Chilton (south of Essex Avenue) is today the south branch of Chilton Street; Essex Avenue continues west as Laurel Lane.
The part's north arrow (about 7 degrees) disagrees with the drawn streets (about 26 degrees); the streets were followed.
Placed from one hand-picked junction (Chilton Street / Essex Avenue / Laurel Lane) with an assumed scale of 8.08 px/ft; low confidence.

50 ft. Four parts divided by heavy lines: 1 top-left, Mine Brook Rd and the mill pond west of town (no junction); 2 top-right, Hoffman Construction Co. quarry (no street); 3 bottom-left, Mine Brook Rd at Depot Pl with the D.L.&W. freight house; 4 bottom-right, Essex Av at Chilton (drawn about 26 deg; its north arrow shows about 7 deg, the streets 26).

Not georeferenced on this sheet: top-left: Mine Brook Road and the mill pond and dam west of town (no street junction; Mine Brook Road and the railroad run parallel without meeting; needs hand placement against aerial imagery (pond, dam) or parcel corners).
Not georeferenced on this sheet: top-right: Hoffman Construction Co. quarry buildings (no street drawn).

sheet-16.description: A strip of Bernards Township east of Bernardsville, along Madisonville Road and Morristown Road. The sheet is turned, with north towards the right of the page: Madisonville Road runs from the top right down to the bottom of the sheet and Morristown Road runs beside it as a long straight road down the right side. Brookside Avenue crosses the top of the sheet and Cottage and Abbe Place cross it lower down, all meeting Tysley Avenue, which runs down the left side. A dash-dot line labelled Bernardsville Bord. Limits on one side and Bernards Township on the other crosses the upper left of the sheet and marks the boundary of the borough. The area is thinly built: small frame dwellings with auto houses on narrow lots along Tysley Avenue and Brookside Avenue, a few larger houses along Madisonville Road, and one large house standing alone on the east side of Madisonville Road near the foot. Most of the large blocks (222, 224, 225) are blank except for dividing lines, and a wedge of land between Madisonville Road and Morristown Road (block 223 and 221) has only one house. A foundation is drawn on Tysley Avenue and the word Arbitrary is printed beside Abbe Place near the foot. Six-inch and eight-inch water pipes follow the roads, with hydrants. Block numbers 221 to 229 are printed. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch.
notes: The sheet is turned: the fit gives a rotation of about 100 degrees, north pointing towards the right of the page.
Tysley Avenue is today Tysley Street and Cottage is Cottage Avenue; Abbe Place is not in the modern street data.
The word Arbitrary is printed near Abbe Place at the foot of the sheet.
Placed from four junctions at the corners of the main block; there is no independent check inside the block.
50 ft. Bernards Township east of town: Madisonville Rd, Brookside Av, Cottage, Tysley Av, Abbe Pl. One part.

sheet-17.description: The centre of Basking Ridge, in Bernards Township, where Oak, Finley Avenue and Maple Avenue meet. The sheet is turned: north points towards the left of the page, so Finley Avenue (Front), the main street, runs across the sheet from left to right and Oak runs up and down. Elm runs across the upper part and Back across the lower part. Henry runs down the right side and continues as Whitnall's Lane at the foot. Maple Avenue and Allen Avenue run in from the upper left, and Finley Avenue also leaves the sheet towards the lower left. The business blocks lie along the north and south sides of Finley Avenue (Front): a post office, the Washington Hotel and a second hotel, stores, an ice house, a garage and auto repair and auto sales buildings, and the Fire Dept. at the corner of Elm and Henry. Churches and public buildings stand around the open triangle where Oak meets Finley Avenue: the Presbyn. Church, whose Grave Yard lies behind it, the Public Library, the Township Hall, Bishop Janes M.E. Church and the Public School. The Presbyn. Parsonage stands on Maple Avenue. Elsewhere the sheet is dwellings with auto houses on 50 to 100 foot lots. Streets are 33 to 60 feet wide, marked on the sheet, and water pipes of four and six inches are drawn with hydrants. A note at the left edge reads No Exposure. Block numbers 55 to 60 and 131, 132 are printed, and the numerals 18 and 19 mark neighbouring sheets. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch.
notes: The sheet is turned: the fit gives a rotation of about -77 degrees, north pointing towards the left of the page.
Oak is today East Oak Street north of Finley Avenue and West Oak Street south of it; Finley Avenue (Front) is South Finley Avenue and the lower-left Finley Avenue is North Finley Avenue.
Elm is today South Maple Avenue and Maple Avenue is North Maple Avenue; Back is Brownlee Place; Henry is Henry Street (identified by position, not by name).
Allen Avenue is not in the modern street data under that name (Allen Street and East Allen Street are further north-west).
The fit has residuals of 2 to 5 m at its six junctions: the modern Oak Street and Finley Avenue lines do not follow the drawn centres closely here.
50 ft. Basking Ridge centre: Oak, Finley Av, Back, Henry, Elm. One part.

sheet-18.description: The southern part of Basking Ridge, along the Finley Avenue and Elm axes. The sheet is nearly upright (north is about 13 degrees to the right of the top). Finley Avenue (Front) runs down the left side and Elm runs down the right, both slightly inclined; Henry crosses the top, Lewis crosses the middle, and Wickenhaver Avenue leaves the middle to the east at the meeting of Elm and Lewis. Prospect Avenue crosses the lower right. The sheet is mainly dwellings, with auto houses and sheds, on lots 50 to 100 feet wide; the west side of Finley Avenue is long, narrow lots running back to a vacant strip noted as Vacant Beyond. Churches are drawn in the block between Finley Avenue and Elm: St. James R.C. Church, with heat by stoves and electric light, near the top beside a row of horse sheds, and St. Marks Episcl. Church lower down. Small trade premises are scattered about: a tin shop at the north end of the block, a blacksmith and wheel wright, a carpenter shop, an undertaker and a print shop. The edge of the sheet at the top shows Henry and the numeral 17 marks the sheet it joins. Water pipes of four and six inches run in the streets, with hydrants at the main corners, and street widths of 33 to 60 feet are written on the sheet. Block numbers 56, 61, 62, 132, 135 and 137 are printed. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and carries the Basking Ridge label.
notes: Finley Avenue (Front) is today South Finley Avenue, Elm is South Maple Avenue, Lewis is Lewis Street, Prospect Avenue is Prospect Avenue and Henry is Henry Street (East Henry Street east of Elm).
Wickenhaver Avenue is not in the modern street data under that name.

Henry Street's north edge lies off the sheet, so the two Henry junctions were hand-picked as the drawn south edge less half the street width; they carry residuals of 4 to 5 m, which may mean the modern Henry line differs from the drawn one.
Placed from three detected junctions and two hand-picked ones; low confidence at the top of the sheet.
50 ft. Basking Ridge: Lewis, Finley, Wickenhaver, Prospect Av, Maple Av. One part.

sheet-19.description: The north end of Basking Ridge, from the Washington Avenue boulevard on the west to Finley Avenue on the east, and from Conkling Avenue at the top to Oak at the foot. Washington Avenue (The Boulevard) is a wide road running down the left side; the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad runs north and south through the middle of the sheet, with the Passenger Station Basking Ridge and a freight house beside Prospect, near the top. Conkling Avenue and Ridge Avenue cross the upper part, Craig and Dayton Avenue the middle, and Lee (Drive), Allen and Oak the lower part, with Hillside Terrace (Avenue) running down between Dayton Avenue and Allen. Finley Avenue runs in from the upper left to the right edge. A large cemetery lies between Washington Avenue and the railroad and takes up the left half of the sheet; it is blank apart from its name. East of the railroad the sheet is dwellings with a few auto houses, and a blacksmith and auto repair shop and an auto repair building along Finley Avenue. Many of the blocks east of Finley Avenue are blank, because the area was sparsely built. The sheet is drawn at the smaller scale of 100 feet to an inch, unlike most of the atlas, and the scale bar at the lower left says so. Water pipes of four and six inches are drawn along most streets. Block numbers 124 to 129, 233 to 239 and 130 are printed. The numeral 17 at the lower right marks the neighbouring sheet. A compass rose at the lower left shows north at the top.
notes: Drawn at 100 feet to an inch; the fit gives about 4.15 px per foot, about 3.6 percent above half the 50 ft sheets' 8.0.

Washington Avenue is today Washington Avenue, Ridge Avenue is Ridge Street, Craig is East Craig Street and West Craig Street, Dayton Avenue is Dayton Street, Finley Avenue is North Finley Avenue, Lee is Lee Place, Hillside Terrace is Hillside Terrace, Allen is Allen Street and Oak is West Oak Street.
The railroad is the Gladstone Branch of the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western; the grade crossing at Ridge Avenue was rejected as a control point (5.7 m from the fit).
Conkling Avenue and Prospect are not placed: no matching modern streets were found.
50 ft. Basking Ridge north: Washington Av, Conkling, Ridge, Craig, Dayton, Lee, Allen, Oak, D.L.&W. depot. One part.
